summary: The milestone completed 6 experiments in 4.7 minutes, including 2 compute-bound runs. Frozen grouped fixed point versus flat control on real outputs was the longest at 4.04 minutes, and the supplied evidence records no compute-bound GPU-idle defect.
bottlenecks_identified: Frozen grouped fixed point versus flat control on real outputs dominated the measured wall time at 4.04 minutes, but the supplied data does not identify the responsible phase.
Disk-mtime reconstruction provides no queue, model-load, inference, verification, or artifact-write timing, so it cannot explain the compute tail.
The point-in-time GPU report does not link accelerator activity or batching opportunities to task phases.
improvements_suggested: Add task-scoped monotonic timers for queue, model load, inference, verification, and artifact write phases.
Emit a compute launch receipt with task identity, model count, selected GPU, and utilization samples from the task window.
Batch 8-16 questions per forward pass when one model serves multiple prompts, then measure the realized speedup.
Schedule independent single-model runs across both GPUs when two ready tasks exist; keep a single-model task on one GPU.
Record DualGPURunner eligibility and selection only when a task loads 2 or more models in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument task phases and task-window GPU use with one compute launch receipt.
Add configurable 8-16 question batching to the single-model inference path.
Dispatch two ready single-model compute tasks to separate GPUs without forcing DualGPURunner.
meta_reflection: The main lesson is an observability gap, not a GPU-idle defect. The next retrospective needs task-owned phase and accelerator receipts before it can attribute the compute tail or quantify savings.
